def: An object type that can be the type of the postfix-expression in a function call expression: function pointers, classes with a member operator(), and classes convertible to function pointers. Pointers to members are not function object types.
The name of a return type followed by a parenthesized, comma-separated list of zero or more argument types, such as int(double, char).
A function object type or a pointer-to-member type; objects of such a type are called callable objects and are uniformly invoked through INVOKE.
An object of a type (a call wrapper type) that holds a target object and supports forwarding calls to it; it at least meets Cpp17MoveConstructible and Cpp17Destructible.
The callable object held by a call wrapper, or an object representing a callable object (such as the pointer in a reference_wrapper).
A sequence of objects and references additionally held by a call wrapper and passed to the target along with the call, such as 1 and 2 in bind_front(f, 1, 2).
Collective name for the target object and bound argument entities of a call wrapper; copying/moving the wrapper is done state entity by state entity.
A call wrapper that accepts an arbitrary argument list and forwards the call arguments by reference (rvalues as rvalue references, lvalues as lvalue references), such as the return value of bind.

An argument forwarding call wrapper that also forwards its state entities according to the cv-qualification and value category of the wrapper itself (cv T& for an lvalue call, cv T&& otherwise); a call is expression-equivalent to its call pattern.

The expression defining the call semantics of a perfect forwarding call wrapper, such as invoke(fd, bound_args..., call_args...); an actual call is expression-equivalent to that expression with its entities replaced by the forwarded references.

A perfect forwarding call wrapper that meets Cpp17CopyConstructible and Cpp17CopyAssignable and whose copy/move constructors and assignments are all non-throwing constexpr functions, such as the return value of mem_fn.

A comparison function object with a member type is_transparent (such as less<>); associative containers use it to enable member template overloads that look up with arguments other than key_type (heterogeneous lookup).

hash<Key> when neither the library nor the user provides a specialization: the type exists, but it is not default constructible, copyable, movable, or assignable, and is not a function object type, so it can be safely detected with SFINAE.
